items.prompt: Which organisation is established by the Chicago Convention?
items.explanation: Article 43 establishes the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), comprising an Assembly, a Council and other necessary bodies. The other organisations are not created by that article. The Convention was signed in 1944; ICAO came into being in 1947.

currentSource.title: Chicago Convention Article 43
currentSource.date: Chicago Convention, ICAO Doc 7300, ninth edition (2006); institutional proposition only
currentSource.note: p.23 para 1.3; p.28 para 1.33. Former p.24 was about law, not establishment. Reviewed 7 November 2026; source scope is limited to the proposition tested.

items.auditReason: Answer b retained; distinguish signing the treaty from ICAO beginning its existence in 1947. Other bodies are not interchangeable with ICAO.

items.prompt: How many Annexes to the Chicago Convention contain ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices, including Safety Management?
items.explanation: There are 19 Annexes. Annex 19 — Safety Management was adopted on 25 February 2013 and became applicable on 14 November 2013. The 2016 course still says 18; that statement was already outdated in 2016. The existence of 19 Annexes does not establish which edition or amendment is operationally applicable.

items.prompt: Under Article 38 of the Chicago Convention, what must a contracting State do if it adopts a practice differing from an international Standard?

options.text: Take no action because Standards are merely optional
Immediately notify ICAO of the difference

items.explanation: Article 38 requires immediate notification to ICAO of differences from international Standards or procedures. It also contains a separate 60-day notification provision for amendments. The AIP publication requirement is a separate AIS obligation, not wording found in Article 38 itself. Recommended Practices and Standards do not have identical legal status.

items.prompt: Which ICAO body meets at least once every three years, with each contracting State entitled to one vote?
items.explanation: The Assembly has the membership and voting rights described in Article 48. The Council is a permanent body responsible to the Assembly (Article 50); the Commission and Secretariat do not replace the Assembly.

items.prompt: An EU Member State publishes an AIP difference from an ICAO Standard covered by SERA. Which statement is correct?

options.text: An AIP entry by itself overrides directly applicable EU law
Difference notification and AIP publication do not by themselves authorise a breach of applicable EU law

items.explanation: Article 38 provides a treaty mechanism for notifying differences, not a general exemption from EU law. SERA Article 3 requires compliance, subject to applicable flexibility safeguards; Article 8 requires compliant additional provisions. Former Article 5 was deleted with effect from 1 May 2025 and must not be cited as an operative current rule. Publishing an AIP entry alone cannot legalise an inconsistent national rule. The course statement that international law does not exist is wrong.

items.prompt: Which certificate does Chicago Convention Article 31 require for an aircraft engaged in international navigation?
items.explanation: Article 31 requires a Certificate of Airworthiness issued or rendered valid by the State of registration. Registration and noise documents serve other purposes; a Minimum Equipment List is not an airworthiness certificate. A certificate is not a guarantee of continuing serviceability for every flight.

items.prompt: An SSR-equipped aircraft encounters an emergency. Which statement correctly describes SERA.13005(a)(1)?

options.text: Always select 7700 regardless of any code previously directed by ATC
Select 7700 unless ATC has previously directed a specified code; even then the pilot may select 7700 whenever there is a specific reason to believe it is the best course of action
Wait for ATC permission before selecting 7700

items.explanation: The default is to select Code 7700 to indicate an emergency. The exception is where ATC has ALREADY directed the pilot to operate on a specified code. Even in that case the pilot may select 7700 whenever there is a specific reason to believe this is the best course of action. This provision does not require waiting for permission. Option a erases the assigned-code exception; c confuses a specific radio-failure procedure with emergency indication; d invents a permission requirement.

items.prompt: Which pair is among the documents required on board by Chicago Convention Article 29 for aircraft of contracting States engaged in international navigation?

options.text: Certificate of Registration and Certificate of Airworthiness

items.explanation: Article 29 lists both certificates, crew licences, the journey log book, a radio station licence if radio apparatus is fitted, and conditional passenger/cargo documents. items.prompt: Two powered aeroplanes are converging at approximately the same level. Neither is towing, landing, overtaking or impaired in manoeuvrability. Which must give way?

options.text: The aircraft with the other on its left
The aircraft with the other on its right
The faster aircraft must always climb
Only an ACAS-equipped aircraft must give way

items.explanation: SERA.3210(c)(2) requires the aircraft with the other on its right to give way. Under (c), it must avoid passing over, under or in front unless it passes well clear and accounts for wake turbulence. The convergence paragraph does not mandate a particular turn direction. The mandatory right turn for head-on encounters is a different rule. Speed and ACAS equipage do not decide this right of way.

items.explanation: SERA.3210(c)(2)(i)–(iii) produces the order balloons → sailplanes → airships → powered aeroplanes. items.prompt: Under SERA.5001, what general flight visibility applies below 10,000 ft AMSL but above the higher of 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain? If the transition altitude is below 10,000 ft AMSL, use FL100 as the upper boundary.
items.explanation: Table S5-1 specifies 5 km flight visibility in this band, with cloud separation of 1,500 m horizontally and 1,000 ft vertically. Its footnote substitutes FL100 for 10,000 ft where the transition altitude is lower. The lower boundary is whichever is higher: 3,000 ft AMSL or 1,000 ft above terrain. This is not the low-level Class F/G reduced-visibility case and does not permit VFR in Class A.

items.prompt: Under SERA.5005, what is the general rule for VFR flight above FL195?

options.text: It is prohibited except under the specified airspace-reservation or authorised-traffic exceptions
It is unrestricted up to FL200
It is permitted only at night

items.explanation: SERA.5005(d)(2) prohibits VFR above FL195 except where an airspace reservation has been established, where practical, or where VFR traffic up to and including FL285 is authorised by the responsible ATS unit under Member State procedures published in the AIP. Paragraph (e) restricts authorisation above FL285 where 1,000 ft vertical separation is applied above FL290. FL200 in the course is not the current SERA threshold; night alone grants no exception.

items.prompt: An aeroplane requests special VFR to take off, land or enter an aerodrome traffic circuit in a control zone. Which set describes the SERA conditions?

options.text: Night flight is always allowed at the pilot’s discretion

ATC clearance; day unless the competent authority permits otherwise; clear of cloud, surface in sight, flight visibility at least 1,500 m, speed at most 140 kt IAS; reported ground visibility at least 1,500 m and ceiling at least 600 ft
A 200 ft ceiling is always sufficient

items.explanation: SERA.5010 requires an ATC clearance. For this aeroplane case, the pilot’s conditions are clear of cloud, surface in sight, flight visibility at least 1,500 m and no more than 140 kt IAS. Day is required unless the competent authority permits otherwise. ATC must not issue the specified take-off/landing/circuit clearance below 1,500 m reported ground visibility or 600 ft ceiling. The aerodrome ground-weather restriction is not a blanket ban on crossing the entire CTR; helicopter exceptions are outside this scenario.

items.prompt: A civil aircraft registered in an EU Member State operates as general air traffic over a non-EU State’s territory. How does SERA describe its territorial application?

options.text: SERA always overrides the overflown State’s published rules
SERA applies to that aircraft only to the extent it does not conflict with rules published by the State having jurisdiction over the territory overflown
Company procedures alone replace the applicable rules

items.explanation: SERA Article 1(2)(b) and SERA.2001 preserve the overflown State’s published rules in a conflict. This does not mean the aircraft’s other applicable obligations disappear. For flight over the high seas, SERA.1001(a) specifies that Annex 2 rules apply without exception, without prejudice to the State-aircraft provisions it identifies. National AIP and applicable authorisations must be checked for actual operations.

items.prompt: Under current SERA definitions, which statement correctly describes a precision approach (PA) procedure?

options.text: It uses lateral guidance only and is necessarily non-precision
It is based on ILS, MLS, GLS or SBAS Cat I and designed for 3D instrument approach operations Type A or B
Any approach with vertical guidance is automatically a PA
Only a ground NDB is needed to provide a PA

items.explanation: Article 2(90)(c) defines PA using those navigation systems and Type A or B 3D operations. Article 2(90)(b) defines APV as a PBN procedure designed for 3D Type A operations. Therefore vertical guidance alone does not make an approach precision. Article 2(89a) distinguishes 2D (lateral only) from 3D (lateral and vertical) operations. The 2016 examples do not define the whole current category.

items.prompt: With the correct QNH set, what vertical reference does an altimeter indicate?

options.text: Indicated altitude above mean sea level
A flight level regardless of pressure setting
Raw static pressure without an altitude reference

items.explanation: QNH references indicated altitude to mean sea level. It does not guarantee true altitude in non-standard temperature or eliminate instrument and pressure-setting errors. QFE references height above its aerodrome or threshold datum; standard pressure is used for flight levels. SERA.8015(eb) distinguishes altitude, flight level and QFE height reporting.

items.prompt: What is the principal purpose of the standard pressure setting, commonly rounded to 1013 hPa?

options.text: To express vertical position as flight levels using a common pressure datum
To show true altitude above mean sea level in every temperature

items.explanation: Flight levels use a common standard pressure datum (SERA Article 2(78): 1013.2 hPa). At or below the transition altitude position is normally expressed as altitude; at or above the transition level as flight level. In the transition layer it is flight level in climb and altitude in descent. A standard-pressure indication is not guaranteed true altitude; it does not measure temperature or abolish QFE.

items.prompt: During a normal descent through the transition level for an approach using QNH, which vertical reference is used in the transition layer?

options.text: Standard pressure until reaching the parking stand

items.explanation: SERA.8015(eb)(1) requires vertical position in the transition layer to be expressed as altitudes when descending, but flight levels when climbing. The flight crew must receive the transition level in time before reaching it, and QNH accompanies the first clearance to an altitude below it unless already provided. This is not a universal claim that every approach uses QNH: local QFE arrangements are separately recognised.

items.prompt: Which SSR Mode A code indicates a general state of emergency under SERA.13005(a)(1)?
items.explanation: 7700 indicates an emergency. This question tests the meaning of the code, not a command to change an assigned code in every emergency. SERA.13005(a)(1) contains the previously-directed-code exception and preserves pilot discretion to select 7700. Code 7600 denotes radio-communication failure; 7500 unlawful interference; 7000 is a conspicuity code subject to the rule and competent-authority provisions.

items.prompt: A VFR flight has a radio-communication failure and attempts to re-establish communication under SERA.14083(a) have failed. Which SSR Mode A code is specified?
items.explanation: SERA.14083(c)(2) specifies Mode A Code 7600 and/or the ADS-B loss-of-communications indication. For this VFR flight, (c)(3) requires continued VMC, landing at the nearest suitable aerodrome and reporting arrival expeditiously to ATS. The different 7601 case in (c)(6) concerns an IFR flight that encounters VMC and whose pilot-in-command decides to continue in VMC. The 7700 assigned-code exception must not be imported into this rule.

items.prompt: An ACAS resolution advisory (RA) conflicts with an ATC manoeuvring instruction. What does SERA require?

options.text: Always follow ATC and ignore the RA

Respond immediately to the RA unless doing so would jeopardise aircraft safety; notify ATC as soon as possible as workload permits, promptly return to the instruction or clearance when the conflict is resolved, and notify ATC when returning
Manoeuvre aggressively on a traffic advisory alone
Switch off the transponder to cancel the conflict

items.explanation: SERA.11014(b) requires following the RA even if it conflicts with an ATC instruction, unless doing so would jeopardise aircraft safety. Do not manoeuvre in the opposite sense; follow modified RAs and limit deviation to what is necessary. Notify ATC as soon as possible as workload permits for a deviation, promptly return to the ATC instruction or clearance when clear of conflict and notify ATC when returning. Do not infer from visual traffic acquisition alone that an RA may be ignored.

items.prompt: Under the SERA Class A classification, which flights are permitted?

options.text: Unrestricted IFR and VFR without clearance

items.explanation: SERA.6001(a)(1) permits IFR flights only in Class A. All flights receive ATC service, are separated from each other, require continuous air-ground voice communication and are subject to ATC clearance. VMC conditions do not create a general right to fly VFR in Class A.

items.prompt: Under SERA Class C rules, which statement is correct?

options.text: VFR flights never need ATC clearance
All flights require ATC clearance; IFR is separated from IFR and VFR; VFR is separated from IFR and receives information about other VFR traffic
VFR receives ATC service only after an IFR conflict arises
No service is provided to VFR flights

items.explanation: SERA.6001(a)(3) provides ATC service to all flights in Class C. VFR flights receive separation from IFR and traffic information about other VFR, with traffic avoidance advice on request. They are not normally separated from one another by the Class C service. All flights require continuous air-ground voice communication and ATC clearance. The course’s p.268 claim that VFR receives ATC only when conflicting with IFR is wrong.

items.prompt: To which flights does SERA.6001 impose the Class C 250 kt IAS limit below 10,000 ft AMSL?

options.text: VFR flights, subject to the stated competent-authority exception

items.explanation: SERA.6001(a)(3) applies the Class C 250 kt IAS limit below 10,000 ft AMSL to VFR flights. An exception requires competent-authority approval for aircraft types that cannot maintain the speed for technical or safety reasons. This paragraph does not impose that Class C limit on IFR flights, but other instructions or rules may still limit their speed.

items.prompt: What does RMZ mean under SERA?

options.text: Radar Minimum Zone with no radio requirement
A zone in which radio use is prohibited

items.explanation: An RMZ is airspace of defined dimensions in which radio carriage and operation are mandatory. Under SERA.6005(a), VFR in designated Class E/F/G and IFR in designated Class F/G must maintain continuous air-ground voice communication watch and establish two-way communication as necessary, unless complying with the ANSP’s alternative provisions. An initial call must be made before entry. An RMZ is not itself a transponder mandatory zone or an ATC-clearance classification.

items.prompt: Under ATS.TR.405(a)(1), which statement correctly gives uncertainty-phase (INCERFA) criteria?

options.text: Every missed communication creates INCERFA after 5 minutes
INCERFA is the phase for failing to land 5 minutes after a landing clearance

No communication within 30 minutes of when one should have been received or of the first unsuccessful contact attempt, whichever is earlier; OR no arrival within 30 minutes of the ETA last notified to or estimated by ATS, whichever is later — unless no doubt exists about the safety of the aircraft and occupants
Only the pilot may initiate INCERFA

items.explanation: ATS.TR.405(a)(1) uses the EARLIER reference for missed communications and the LATER reference for arrival. The no-doubt safety exception applies. ATS must immediately notify the rescue coordination centre when the aircraft is considered in the relevant emergency phase, subject to ATS.TR.420(a). The separate ALERFA landing criterion is failure to land within 5 minutes of the ESTIMATED TIME OF LANDING after being cleared to land, with communication not re-established — not simply 5 minutes after clearance issue. The ALERFA triggers in (a)(2)(i)–(iv), including this landing case, do not apply when evidence exists that would allay apprehension as to the safety of the aircraft and occupants.

items.prompt: Rank these ATS emergency phases from lower to higher severity. This is a severity ranking, not a compulsory sequence of delays.
items.explanation: The severity order is uncertainty → alert → distress. ATS.TR.405 contains independent triggers: for example, known or believed unlawful interference can trigger ALERFA, and evidence of an imminent forced landing can trigger DETRESFA. ATS need not mechanically wait through every earlier phase before acting on stronger evidence.

items.prompt: How far apart are the common effective dates in the AIRAC system?
items.explanation: ICAO Annex 15 section 6.2.1 uses common effective dates at 28-day intervals. This is a cycle interval, not the same as a distribution or receipt deadline. EU AIS.OR.505 separately requires information to reach recipients at least 28 days before the effective date. The course’s blanket 42-day distribution statement must not be confused with that separate requirement.

items.prompt: What is the sole objective of a civil aviation safety investigation under Regulation (EU) No 996/2010?

options.text: To prevent future accidents and incidents without apportioning blame or liability
To automatically replace the aircraft’s airworthiness certificate

items.explanation: Articles 1 and 5(6) make accident and incident prevention the objective, not apportioning blame or liability. Safety investigations remain independent of, separate from and without prejudice to judicial or administrative proceedings. This does not mean those separate proceedings cannot take place.

items.prompt: A fatal civil airliner accident occurs in an EU Member State and falls within Regulation (EU) No 996/2010. Which State has the initial territorial responsibility for the safety investigation?

options.text: The State in which the accident occurred
Only the aircraft commander’s home State

items.explanation: Under Article 5(1), the investigation takes place in the Member State of occurrence; Article 4 requires an independent safety investigation authority. Under Article 6(2), the task may be delegated to another safety investigation authority by mutual agreement. Other States can participate under the applicable rules. This scenario is a fatal airliner accident, so the limited no-fatal/no-serious-injury small-aircraft derogation in Article 5(5) is not relevant.

items.prompt: In EASA CS-ADR-DSN Issue 7, F.370(c), what minimum separation is specified for an isolated aircraft parking position from other parking positions, buildings or public areas?
items.explanation: The certification specification says the position should be at the maximum practicable distance and in any case never less than 100 m from other parking positions, buildings or public areas. This is an aerodrome design specification, not a stand-alone universally applicable pilot operating law. GM1 advises avoiding underground utilities. Actual aerodrome arrangements and certification basis must be checked.
